# qompack micro-benchmark baseline — recorded by SP-01, the first checkpoint (V1).
#
# Recorded with the command V1-VERIFY §7 P-13 uses for comparison, but at -count 10 rather than
# -count 5: benchstat needs at least 6 samples to report a confidence interval, so a 5-sample
# baseline can only ever be compared point-to-point.
#
#     go test -run '^$' -bench . -benchmem -count 10 -p 1 ./...
#
# Host: Windows 11, Intel Core Ultra 7 155H, NTFS. This host has high per-syscall filesystem
# latency — an isolated fsync measures ~2.1 ms and a create+write+close ~0.65 ms. The two
# I/O-bound entries below are dominated by that, and will look very different on the Linux CI
# runners. Treat a large improvement there as a change of machine, not a change of code; the
# allocation columns are the platform-independent half of this file.
#
# Budgets from SP-01's Definition of Done item 16, and how this recording compares:
#
#     BenchmarkHistogram_Observe        < 100 ns/op    MET      19.09n ±13%
#     BenchmarkConfigLoad_ColdNoFiles   < 2 ms/op      MET      950.5µ ± 6%
#     BenchmarkHookNoop_InProcess       < 3 ms/op      MISSED   5.322m ± 4%
#     BenchmarkPathsWriteAtomic_4KB     < 2 ms/op      MISSED   4.718m ± 8%
#
# Both misses are filesystem-bound on this host rather than algorithmic, and both are recorded
# honestly rather than restated to fit:
#
#   - PathsWriteAtomic_4KB cannot reach 2 ms here by construction. §4.6 requires an fsync of the
#     staged file before the rename, and a bare fsync alone costs ~2.1 ms on this machine — more
#     than the whole budget, before WriteAtomic does any work of its own.
#
#   - HookNoop_InProcess spends its time on syscalls the wave-0 hook repeats on every single
#     invocation: EnsureLayout's directory creation, a fresh logger open, and the observation
#     append. Allocations are flat at 2300/op across every sample, so this is I/O, not garbage.
#     SP-05's resident daemon is what removes it — caching the layout and the logger is precisely
#     the work budget B-A (hook p99 < 15 ms) assumes has already been done. This number is the
#     headroom measurement the benchmark exists to provide, and it says the no-op path currently
#     consumes about a third of B-A before SP-08 observes anything at all.
#
goos: windows
goarch: amd64
pkg: github.com/qompack/qompack/internal/cli
cpu: Intel(R) Core(TM) Ultra 7 155H

# ── SP-02 (L7 replay harness) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Recorded with the same command and on the same host as the SP-01 block above:
#
#     go test -run '^$' -bench . -benchmem -count 10 -p 1 ./...
#
# Budgets from plans/V2-SP-02-replay-harness-belady-baseline.md §14, and how this recording
# compares. All of these are algorithmic rather than I/O-bound, so unlike the two SP-01 misses
# they should hold on the Linux CI runners too:
#
#     BenchmarkBeladyDetail_400Turns        <= 250 ms/op   MET   ~1.6 ms/op, 0.68 MB/op (E-2)
#     BenchmarkCompare_400Actions           <=  20 ms/op   MET   ~2.0 ms/op, 0.19 MB/op (E-4)
#     BenchmarkBreakpointOPT_256Candidates  <=  15 ms/op   MET   ~1.1 ms/op             (E-5)
#
# E-2's allocation budget is 96 MB; the measured 0.68 MB/op is two orders of magnitude under it,
# because pruning every never-demanded block leaves the DP a few hundred candidates rather than
# the few thousand blocks a 400-turn session actually holds.

goos: windows
goarch: amd64
pkg: github.com/qompack/qompack/internal/eval
